meta.title: otaviom — narrative landing pages, product and infrastructure
meta.description: I design narrative landing pages, build the product behind them and run the infrastructure that puts both online. Six pieces, three technical cases and a pipeline I run myself.
meta.ogTitle: otaviom — landing pages that tell a story
meta.ogDescription: Scrolling becomes the camera. Six corridors, three products and the infrastructure holding it all up.
hero.title: I design pages that tell a story. And I build what runs behind them.
hero.sub: Landing pages where scrolling is the camera, products with a real backend, and the infrastructure that puts both online. The whole thing, made by one person.
scrub.line1: The scroll doesn't move the page. It walks down the corridor.
scrub.line2: Every frame is the video being seeked to the exact position of your scrollbar.
do.title: Three skills the rest of this page backs up.
do.s1.title: Landing pages with a story
do.s1.body: The whole page is a walk-through: the background video advances as the visitor scrolls, captions change with each scene, and the offer arrives at the end of the corridor. Copy, art direction, animation and the video all come from here.
do.s1.stack: HTML · CSS · JS, no framework · Range-based scrubbing
do.s2.title: Product and backend
do.s2.body: For when the page needs something behind it: API, database, authentication, third-party integration, internal dashboard. I would rather ship something small that stands up than something large that wobbles.
do.s2.stack: Node · TypeScript · Next · Postgres · Cloudflare Workers · D1
do.s3.title: Infrastructure and my own pipeline
do.s3.body: I operate what I deliver. Containers, reverse proxy, tunnel, deploys on the edge. Plus a local pipeline that generates the story videos, with no stock footage and no platform credits.
do.s3.stack: Docker · Caddy · Cloudflare Tunnel · Pages · ComfyUI

cases.title: Where the work doesn't show on screen.
cases.sub: Real products, described for what they are. No invented metrics and no fake dashboard screenshots.
cases.ata.problem: A recorded meeting doesn't turn into knowledge: nobody rewatches two hours of video to find the decision made at minute 74.
cases.ata.built: The recording backend: a bot joins the meeting on Zoom, Meet or Teams, records it, transcribes it and returns a summary, an action plan and a mind map. Every meeting gets its own chat, and a general chat answers across all of them, always citing the source.
cases.ata.stack: Node · TypeScript · Postgres + pgvector · Firebase Auth
cases.ata.now: A v2 rewrite in a monorepo: Next 16, Expo, custom design tokens and i18n. Work in progress, not shipped.
cases.dropi.problem: A shipping scraper collected products all day, but checking what it had brought in meant opening the database by hand.
cases.dropi.built: An internal dashboard to inspect the collection: search, filters, product detail and the history of every run. Packaged in Docker with a healthcheck, with unit and end-to-end tests running before each deploy.
cases.dropi.stack: Next 14 App Router · Drizzle · Postgres 16 · NextAuth · TanStack Query · Vitest · Playwright · Docker
cases.niko.problem: The music bots on my Discord server kept dying or turning into paid subscriptions.
cases.niko.built: My own bot, with a queue, button controls instead of memorised commands, and an automatic exit when nobody is left listening. A small, honest project: it exists because I use it.
behind.title: The videos and the servers are mine too.
behind.b1.title: The video starts here
behind.b1.body: None of the corridors on this page came from a stock library. All of them were generated on my own machine, 15 seconds at 720p per piece, then re-encoded with dense keyframes, which is what makes it possible to seek the video frame by frame as you scroll.
behind.b2.title: And ships through my homelab
behind.b2.body: I run a server at home with the services in containers, a reverse proxy in front and a tunnel to expose whatever needs an external link. That's where clients review the pieces before they go live. Anything public lives on Cloudflare's edge.
behind.b2.stack: Docker · Caddy · Cloudflare Tunnel · Pages · D1
behind.b3.title: One detail that breaks everything
behind.b3.body: Video that responds to scrolling requires the server to return chunks of the file on demand. Static hosting tends to return the whole file instead, and the scrub freezes, with no console error and no warning. Every page here ships with an edge function just to solve that.
about.lead: I'm José Otávio, a freelance developer and designer based in Brazil. I sign my work as otaviom.
about.p1: I started with code and ended up designing, because shipping a beautiful page that never goes live (or one that goes live and convinces nobody) only solves half the problem. These days I take the whole piece: the idea, the narrative, the video, the code and the server.
about.p2: I work alone and I like small, well-finished things. If a project needs a team, I say so before we start.
